summary: Agent Jones flings the door wide and steps inside the flooded Executive Office, walking through puddles in the carpet. Amid the rushing water and alarms, Agent Smith hears a noise and realizes the severity of the assault. He glances toward the glass wall as a helicopter drops into view, with Neo in the back bay aiming a mounted.50 machine gun. Smith says "No." The gun fires and bullets explode through the window in shattering glass as the Agents rush for their weapons, yet Neo is too close and the.50 caliber too fast, riddling the space. Agent Jones takes the first shots, jack-knifing back with blood and a flash of light; then Agent Brown, still firing as he falls; and finally Agent Smith. With the Agents down, Neo watches Morpheus, desperate to force him to move, shouting "Get up, Morpheus! Get up!" Neo then grabs a Neo seizes a climbing rope and fastens one end to his harness.

event_hint.one_line: Neo gunships the Executive Office, kills the three Agents, and moves to rescue Morpheus.

minds.wants: To identify and name the threat the moment it registers, reasserting control over a situation that has breached the Agents' sanctuary.
minds.feels: A cold, sharpening clarity — the chaotic noise resolves into a single understood fact: this is not a contained intrusion but a serious, lethal attack. The realization carries the weight of something genuinely new, not just more of the same.
minds.shows: A single, flat, almost understated word — "No." — delivered as he turns to face the window, no alarm in his voice.
minds.basis: The text states outright that 'amid the gushing water and the alarms, Agent Smith catches a noise and realizes how grave the assault is,' then has him turn to the window and say 'No' as the helicopter drops into view. The change of knowledge axis in what_changes confirms a shift from chaos to comprehension.

believes_about.belief: That this is a manageable, containable problem — that a human, even an unusually capable one, can be stopped once identified.
believes_about.wrong_because: The sound he 'understands' is precisely the arrival of a threat that will kill all three of them within seconds; his composure ('No') presumes a contest he has already lost.

minds.wants: To close with and overwhelm the target — to finish what he began on the roof.
minds.feels: Predatory momentum and confidence carried straight from the rooftop, where he had Neo helpless at gunpoint; the flooded office is just another hunting ground he enters without hesitation.
minds.shows: Physical aggression without words — throwing the door open, striding through the puddles, then going for his weapon the instant gunfire erupts.
minds.basis: He enters first and unhesitating, 'He strides through the waterlogged carpet.,' and is 'hit first' when the Agents draw. His characterization in sc-163 — charging, taunting Neo as 'Only human,' raising his gun for the kill — establishes the aggressive, confident posture he carries into this room.

believes_about.belief: That Neo remains the outmatched human he had pinned on the roof — prey, not an executioner.
believes_about.wrong_because: Neo now controls a .50 caliber mounted gun from a helicopter, reversing the power relationship entirely; Jones is killed first precisely because he is leading the charge into that new reality.

minds.wants: To return fire and suppress the attacker — to do the job an Agent does under assault.
minds.feels: Reflexive, trained combat response; no time for assessment, only reaction.
minds.shows: Drawing and firing his weapon even as he is being cut down — 'his weapon still spitting bullets as he drops.'
minds.basis: The text shows him firing as he dies, the only behavioral data available; there is no dialogue or interior access to differentiate him, so the reading is limited to the observable combat reflex.

minds.wants: To confront and stop the threat head-on rather than be caught off-guard.
minds.feels: The same cold command as the moment of recognition — he meets the attack standing, choosing direct confrontation.
minds.shows: He turns to face the window and stands to confront the gun rather than take cover; he is 'finally' the last of the three to fall.
minds.basis: His 'No' and turn toward the window, and the what_changes note that he goes 'from standing and confronting the threat' to 'shot dead.' He is positioned as the one who understood first and faces it last.

believes_about.belief: That understanding the threat grants him some measure of control over it.
believes_about.wrong_because: His hard-won comprehension changes nothing about the outcome — he still dies, and last, underscoring that knowledge did not equal mastery.

minds.wants: To get Morpheus out alive — right now — by any force of will or action available.
minds.feels: Desperate, focused urgency mixed with helplessness: he has just cleared the room of its guardians, yet the one thing he needs — Morpheus moving — he cannot command.
minds.shows: First a silent, intense effort — 'staring... trying to will him into action' — then breaking into shouted commands, then wordlessly grabbing the climbing rope to act himself.
minds.basis: The text gives both the mute, willing stare and the shouted 'Get up, Morpheus! Get up!' followed immediately by him attaching the rope to his harness — a shift from trying to make Morpheus move to preparing to move him himself. This continues his rescue drive from the rooftop ('we have to keep moving') and the whole event's objective.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus can be roused — that a shout, or sheer will, will pull him back to his feet.
believes_about.wrong_because: Morpheus does not respond (the text shows Neo 'trying to will him into action' and having to shout), forcing Neo to abandon persuasion and physically extract him — Morpheus is not reachable by will alone in this moment.

connects_back: Agent Jones carrying his rooftop dominance (sc-163) into this room, where he enters first and dies first.
The rooftop near-death at Jones's hands (sc-163) — Neo's reversal from prey to the one wielding the .50 is the payoff of that sequence.
Trinity loading the helicopter pilot program (sc-164/165) — the means by which Neo reaches this window at all.
The ongoing rescue objective that has driven Neo and Trinity since the lobby assault (ev-037).
sets_up: Neo's physical extraction of the still-unresponsive Morpheus from the office via the climbing rope.
The Agents' return — having been 'destroyed' rather than permanently killed — to pursue the rescue.
The escalation of Neo's capability beyond ordinary human limits, established by his rooftop movement in sc-163 and now by his overwhelming of the Agents.
dramatic_function: It converts the rescue mission from a desperate scramble into a decisive, dominant strike — the attackers who seemed untouchable are shown to be killable — while pivoting the scene's tension from external combat to the intimate, unresolved problem of reaching an unresponsive Morpheus, so the climax becomes about will versus helplessness rather than firepower.
